The project is under the corporate social responsibility scheme of the IRFC. The agreement was signed by S.

stories.title: Chef Kunal Kapur shares the perfect way to eat winter greens with his comforting saag paneer recipe
stories.summary: Chef Kunal Kapur incorporates five leafy greens: mustard, spinach, bathua, methi and radish leaves in his simple but indulgent saag paneer recipe. Winter is the season of greens, and while spinach often takes the spotlight, there are many other leafy vegetables in Indian home kitchens that deserve just as much appreciation.

stories.title: TIFR Hyderabad, CMC Vellore join hands to advance metabolic health research
stories.summary: The Advanced Research Unit on Metabolism, Development and Aging (ARUMDA) at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Hyderabad, has strengthened India’s metabolic health research capabilities with the inauguration of a state-of-the-art Human Metabolic Chamber (HMC) at the Christian Medical College, Vellore. The facility, inaugurated by Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava, marks a milestone in the collaboration between the two institutions to advance research on diabetes, obesity, malnutrition and age-related diseases.

stories.title: Kate Middleton tells brother James she never rang the bell after cancer treatment in new documentary
stories.summary: Kate Middleton revealed that she never rang the bell to mark the end of her cancer treatment, sharing the emotional detail in the trailer for her upcoming documentary Heal. In the trailer released on Saturday, the Princess of Wales is seen speaking to her brother James Middleton about the tradition of ringing a bell after completing cancer treatment at the Royal Marsden Hospital.

stories.title: Bausch + Lomb's eye-drop drug fails to reduce pain after laser surgery in trial
stories.summary: Bausch + Lomb said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study. However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing.

stories.title: Sandpapergate scandal: AB de Villiers makes new claim about Australian ball-tampering
stories.summary: Former South African batsman AB de Villiers has alleged Australia engaged in ball-tampering from the first match of their 2018 "Sandpapergate" tour of South Africa. de Villiers alleged in a post on his YouTube channel that the ball-tampering, which culminated in Cameron Bancroft being caught using sandpaper in the third Test in Cape Town, actually began in the first Test in Durban.

stories.summary: Former India players Bembem Devi, Bentla D'Coth, Jo Paul Ancheri and Bruno Coutinho were on Monday elected as four Sportspersons of Merit (SOMs) to become members of the General Body of the All India Football Federation (AIFF) for the December 20 polls. stories.summary: India captain Shubman Gill has questioned the continued prohibition on using saliva to shine the ball , arguing that it further tilts the balance towards batters, particularly when pitches offer little assistance. Gill’s remarks came after India’s first Test against New Zealand at Basin Reserve ended in a draw on Monday, with the hosts batting out the final day to finish at 239 for five.

stories.title: Tyson Fury reveals he has schizophrenia; wife Paris opens up on ‘voices in his head’
stories.summary: For Tyson Fury, the years following his 2015 victory over Wladimir Klitschko brought a collapse that few outside his inner circle fully understood. Behind the scenes, the heavyweight champion was battling severe mental health problems, hearing voices and becoming increasingly convinced that he and his family were in danger.

stories.title: Is Marquez MotoGP's greatest of all time?
stories.summary: As Marc Marquez ascended a staircase, the silhouette of a goat matched his every step. It was a nod to his increasing - or solidified, depending on who you ask - status as MotoGP's 'greatest of all time' (GOAT). In winning the 2026 championship in Portugal on Sunday, Spain's Marquez secured his eighth overall title, the first per son in the modern era to achieve this accolade.

stories.title: Foreman Texas Estate Sale: Longtime home lists for $6 million; 50-car garage and grill-ad kitchen
stories.summary: George Foreman’s longtime Texas home has hit the market for $6 million, nearly 19 months after the boxing legend died at age 76. The Huffman property includes an 11,968-square-foot mansion and a climate-controlled garage with room for more than 50 cars. stories.summary: England's Marco Penge birdied the first extra hole in a four-man play-off to win the RSM Classic in Georgia and secure his PGA Tour card for 2027. Penge's five-under 65 in a delayed final round at the Sea Island Resort's Seaside Course had left him tied at 16 under overall, with American duo Max Greyserman and Michael Thorbjornsen, and China's Li Haotong.

stories.title: 49ers cut ties with Brandon Aiyuk after WR’s two-year stretch without playing a game
stories.summary: The San Francisco 49ers have cut ties with disgruntled wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, freeing the former second-team All-Pro to join another team. stories.title: Raghuvanshi’s show guides Mumbai to commanding win over Chhattisgarh in the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 cricket tournament
stories.summary: On his Indian Premier League (IPL) home ground, Angkrish Raghuvanshi scored a career-best 63-ball 84 not out as Mumbai cruised to a commanding nine-wicket win over Chhattisgarh in an Elite Group-D match of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy T20 tournament at the Eden Gardens here on Sunday. Chhattisgarh, asked to bat, scored 159, which the star-studded Mumbai side achieved with seven balls to spare.

stories.title: Shubman Gill explains why 'very good friend' Mohammed Siraj was dropped for New Zealand Test
stories.summary: India Test captain Shubman Gill defended the decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI after the first Test against New Zealand ended in a draw on Monday. stories.summary: One between two sides looking to recover from embarrassing home defeats, another a match-up between two teams looking to build on decent away victories. stories.title: Daryl Mitchell, Phillips defy India as Wellington Test ends in a draw
stories.summary: India picked up five wickets in New Zealand's second innings but ran out of time as Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Philips' stubborn resistance denied them a win at the Basin Reserve. With the pitch offering little assistance, Mitchell and Phillips dug in to secure a draw. The second Test of the two-match series will be played in Christchurch from Friday.

stories.title: Alex Ovechkin Gives Children Battling Cancer a Special Day at the Capitals' Training Facility
stories.summary: During his final NHL season, Alex Ovechkin created a memorable experience for children affected by cancer at the Washington Capitals’ training facility. The young fans got an opportunity to step onto the ice, take shots from his famous scoring spot, and spend an unforgettable afternoon with the hockey legend.

stories.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
stories.summary: Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years Maxx Morando during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California. Photos of the wedding on Saturday show the ceremony took place by a swimming pool with the pair standing under an arch covered in white flowers. The singer's mother, Tish Cyrus, and sister, Noah Cyrus, were in attendance, Entertainment Tonight reported.

stories.title: 8th Pay Commission: Civilian defence staff seek 6% annual increment, OPS and 50% DA merger— 13 key demands explained

stories.title: Who is Sugandha Hiremath? Meet businesswoman at centre of Kalyani family’s ₹1 lakh crore ancestral wealth dispute
stories.summary: Sugandha Hiremath, sister of Bharat Forge chairman Baba Kalyani, is at the centre of a high-profile inheritance dispute involving the Kalyani family’s ancestral wealth , estimated at more than ₹ 1 lakh crore. The legal battle, which has dragged on across judicial forums, involves claims over family assets, properties and stakes in companies linked to the Pune-based industrial family.

stories.title: From kala pani to Rikers, history of island prisons and the waters used to lock people in | HT Explainers
stories.summary: In Alexandre Dumas's The Count of Monte Cristo, the young sailor Edmond Dantès works out where the gendarmes are rowing him only as the boat nears the Château d'If, a fortress on a rock off Marseille. stories.title: Everyday Explained: Why do wooden doors swell during monsoons and become difficult to shut?
stories.summary: From humidity to moisture absorption, an expert explains why wooden doors swell during monsoons and become difficult to shut. A door that closes effortlessly one day may suddenly start getting stuck in its frame when the rains arrive. This common monsoon inconvenience is not necessarily a sign of poor carpentry or damaged hinges.

stories.title: Who is Artemis Patrick? Meet Sephora CEO as she reveals why she once refused to work at the beauty company
stories.summary: Sephora CEO Artemis Patrick has revealed that she once rejected a job offer from the beauty retailer because she was unwilling to follow its strict dress code. The incident dates back to 1998, when Sephora was a small perfumery recently acquired by luxury group LVMH. At the time, the company required its employees to wear outfits in only three colours: black, white or grey.

stories.title: What happened to Jaylen Harrell? Police reveal alleged Uber driver assault before Titans star’s crash
stories.summary: Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell is facing questions after a serious car accident in Tampa, Florida, left him hospitalized with major injuries. According to the Tampa Police Department, the 24-year-old allegedly assaulted his Uber driver while riding in the back seat on Friday morning, November 20. Police say the driver lost control after the reported incident, hitting another vehicle before crashing into a utility pole.

stories.title: What next after COP31: Countries return to table at UN's Bonn talks in June 2027 | HT Explainers
stories.summary: The United Nations’ mid-year climate meetings in Bonn in June 2027 are the first formal chance for governments to return to the disputes over fossil fuels and money for poorer countries that left COP31 without a deal, five months before the next summit in Ethiopia.

stories.title: Is air pollution putting India’s frontline workers at risk? | In Focus Podcast
stories.summary: With the onset of winter, air pollution levels in Indian cities have touched alarming highs once again. While discussions around air pollution often centre on soaring AQI levels, smog and measures to curb vehicular emissions, what tends to get overlooked is its disproportionate impact on the most vulnerable groups, particularly those whose jobs expose them to polluted air for prolonged periods.

stories.title: Can Congress Turn Anti-AAP Sentiment Into A Comeback in Punjab?
stories.summary: On November 4, Rahul Gandhi returned to Punjab, a State where the Congress party has historically known how to sway voters and win elections. Launching the campaign for the Punjab Assembly elections in Sangrur, an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) stronghold, Rahul attacked the AAP’s record in government and argued that Punjab needed a government that worked for the State rather than being “run from Delhi”.

stories.summary: A routine repair job takes a disturbing turn in GTA 6 when Jason discovers something unusual while trying to clear Mandy’s blocked sink. Players have begun examining the scene closely, and one detail has sparked a chilling theory: the object lodged inside the pipe could be a human finger.

stories.title: Is your breathing at risk? A pulmonologist shares signs that your COPD might be in a flare-up
stories.summary: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a progressive lung condition that makes breathing difficult due to restricted airflow in the lungs. It includes conditions such as chronic bronchitis and emphysema. One of the major challenges for people living with COPD is the occurrence of flare-ups, also known as exacerbations.

stories.title: Who is taking part in France's recent street protests?
stories.summary: Student demonstrators demanding better conditions have been joined by yellow vest activists and others, angry about the rising cost of living. stories.title: Karthigai Deepam row explained: What is Deepathoon dispute, and why has Tamil Nadu challenged Supreme Court order?
